rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L04.html Proposition 1.3 and proof (lines 77-84); paragraph after it (line 86)
rows.evidence: unchanged since a2a631a (git diff checked); round-24 evidence: Re-derived: by stationarity T Var(dbar) = T^-1 sum_{s,t} gamma(t - s) = sum_{|h| < T} (1 - |h|/T) gamma(h). The terms converge pointwise to gamma(h) and are dominated by |gamma(h)|, which is summable by (i), so T Var(dbar) -> sigma^2_LR. Under H0, DM = (sqrt T dbar/sigma_LR)(sigma_LR/sigma-hat_LR): the first factor -> N(0,1) by (ii); the second -> 1 in probability by (iii) and continuity of x -> sqrt(sigma^2_LR/x) at sigma^2_LR > 0; Slutsky gives the limit, so both the one-sided and two-sided tests have asymptotic level alpha. If mu > 0: DM = sqrt T mu/sigma-hat + sqrt T (dbar - mu)/sigma-hat, where the second term is O_p(1) and the first diverges. Assumptions complete and proof complete. Line 86: (iii) needs l to grow with T, and more slowly than T. unchanged since a2a631a (git diff checked); round-24 evidence: Re-checked from scratch (L04 line 100). Combination error e0 - lambda(e0 - e1); MSE = E[e0^2] - 2 lambda E[e0(e0 - e1)] + lambda^2 E[(e0 - e1)^2] (quadratic A - 2 lambda B + lambda^2 C, minimised at B/C with minimum A - B^2/C, checked numerically); lambda* = E[e0(e0 - e1)]/E[(e0 - e1)^2]; encompassing iff E[e0(e0 - e1)] = 0. The repaired example reads 'If both forecasts are unbiased, with mean squared error s^2 and error correlation rho < 1': unbiased means E e = 0, so E[e0 e1] = rho s^2, E[e0(e0 - e1)] = s^2(1 - rho) > 0, E[(e0 - e1)^2] = 2 s^2(1 - rho), lambda* = 1/2, MSE of the equal-weight combination = (2 s^2 + 2 rho s^2)/4 = s^2(1 + rho)/2 < s^2. Simulation (2,000,000 draws, s^2 = 1.69, rho = 0.3, verify8 inline numpy check): lambda* = 0.4995, E[e0(e0 - e1)] = 1.1832 against s^2(1 - rho) = 1.1830, combination MSE 1.0966 against 1.0985. A biased pair (means 1.0 and -0.8, correlation 0.3) gives E[e0(e0 - e1)] = 2.50 against the formula's 1.40, so the added hypothesis is necessary and sufficient for the stated formula. The conclusion 'a DM test would find nothing to choose between them, and the combination beats both' follows (equal MSE gives E d = 0). rows.evidence: unchanged since a2a631a (git diff checked); round-24 evidence: Re-derived at 7ff7507 from the printed paragraph; scripts remark35_limits.py (output remark35_limits.out) and signflip_check.py (outputs signflip_probe2.out, signflip_T2000.out). (1) Given the data, the reference law of T^(-1/2) sum_t eps_t d_t has variance T^(-1) sum_t d_t^2 (eps_t = +-1 i.i.d., mean 0, variance 1), so (H1) gives gamma(0). (2) The reference law is symmetric about 0, so its 95% quantile of |.| equals its 97.5% quantile of the signed sum; under (H2) both tend to the 0.975 quantile of N(0, gamma(0)). (3) Quantile identity checked numerically (remark35_limits.out section 1, g = 2.5): 95% quantile of |N(0,g)| = sqrt(g) z_0.975 = 3.0989751615, 97.5% quantile of N(0,g) = 3.0989751615 (equal); z_0.975 = 1.9599639845 (so 1.96 is the 97.5% quantile of N(0,1)). The literal misreading (97.5% quantile of |N(0,1)| = 2.2414027276) is not what the sentence now says. (4) (H3) gives T^(-1/2) sum d_t -> N(0, sigma2_LR); sigma2_LR/gamma(0) = (1+phi)/(1-phi) = 3 at phi = 0.5 and 1.857142857 at phi = 0.3 (remark35_limits.out section 2: direct sums over |h| <= 4000 agree with the closed form). (5) The limit: 2(1 - Phi(1.96 sqrt(gamma0/sigma2))) = 0.2577998945 at phi = 0.5 (page form 2(1 - Phi(1.132)) = 0.2576344344, rounds to 0.258) and 0.1503640418 at phi = 0.3 (page form 2(1 - Phi(1.438)) = 0.1504340541, rounds to 0.150) (remark35_limits.out section 3). Monte Carlo (signflip_check.py, Gaussian AR(1), phi = 0.5, unit innovations): at T = 2000, R = 3000, K = 499 random sign patterns, rejection rate 0.2523 (MC SE 0.0079) against the limit 0.2578 (signflip_T2000.out); conditional 95% quantile of T^(-1/2)|sum eps d| at T = 20000, K = 40000 is 2.292406 against 1.96 sqrt(T^(-1) sum d^2) = 2.285884 (within the quantile's Monte Carlo error, about 0.01). Advisory, not a failure: the last step (Slutsky with a continuous limit law at the cut-off) is used without being named; naming it would make the proof checkable at a glance.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L03.html Lemma 2.3 (line 102) and its proof; card S7-c217
rows.evidence: unchanged since a2a631a (git diff checked); round-24 evidence: Re-derived. (a) p_(k) <= kq/m iff at least k p-values are <= kq/m: if p_(k) <= kq/m then p_(1..k) are all <= kq/m, so N(k) >= k; if N(k) >= k then the k-th smallest is <= kq/m. Hence R = max{k : N(k) >= k}. (b) If R >= 1, a rejected H_i has p_i <= p_(R) <= Rq/m. Conversely, if p_i <= Rq/m but p_i = p_(j) with j > R, then p_(j) <= Rq/m <= jq/m, so N(j) >= j, contradicting the maximality of R; the zero case is handled (N(1) >= 1 forces R >= 1). (c) Raising a p-value can only lower each N(k), so the largest k with N(k) >= k cannot increase. Numerical spot check (scratch py/spotchecks_r12.py): for 2,000 random p-vectors (m = 10, q = 0.05, mixed scales) the BH rejection set equals {i : p_i <= R q/m} with R = max{k : N(k) >= k} (0 violations), and R does not increase when one randomly chosen p-value is raised (0 violations). Ties: the proof uses the k-th smallest p-value, so ties do not change the count.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L03.html Proposition 5.3 (line 281) and its proof; card S7-c218
rows.evidence: unchanged since a2a631a (git diff checked); round-24 evidence: Re-derived for rho in [0,1). Given z_i = t, the joint Gaussian (W, z_i) gives W | z_i = t ~ N(sqrt(rho)(t - mu_i), 1 - rho), stochastically increasing in t for rho >= 0 (the constant case rho = 0 is trivially monotone). The other coordinates are z_j = sqrt(rho) W + sqrt(1-rho) eps_j + mu_j with eps_j independent of (W, z_i), so P(z in D' | z_i = t) = E[g(W) | z_i = t], g non-increasing for a decreasing D' (translating all z_j by a common amount). Hence t -> P(z in D' | z_i = t) is non-increasing, which is PRDS (Definition 5.1) on every subset. Numerical spot check (scratch py/spotchecks_r12.py, Monte Carlo 600,000 draws, rho = 0.5, m = 3, D = {p_2 >= 1/2, p_3 >= 1/2}, an increasing set in p-space): P(D | z_1 near t) falls from 0.556 at t = -1 to 0.033 at t = 2 (non-increasing in t), and P(D | p_1 near u) rises from 0.054 at u = 0.05 to 0.708 at u = 0.95 (non-decreasing in u): the PRDS inequality holds in the numerical check. (An earlier attempt used the z-increasing set {z_2 > 0, z_3 > 0}; that set is not an increasing set of p-values, so it was discarded.)

rows.evidence: unchanged since a2a631a (git diff checked); round-24 evidence: Re-derived from Definition 4.1 (L04.html lines 268–275: V_K = max_k sqrt(T) dbar_k; V*_{K,j} = max_k sqrt(T)(dbar*_{k,j} - dbar_k) with one index sequence per draw shared by all strategies; p-hat = mean_j 1{V*_{K,j} >= V_K}). (a) Adding any strategy adds one term to each maximum: V*_{K+1,j} = max(V*_{K,j}, term_j) >= V*_{K,j} for every draw j. (b) If its statistic s = sqrt(T) dbar_{K+1} is not the largest (s <= V_K), then V_{K+1} = V_K. (c) Hence with the same draws p-hat can only rise, and rejection at alpha (p-hat <= alpha) can only be lost. Numerical check of (a)–(c) with the Definition 4.1 procedure, seed 20261020, 300 trials, T = 120, B = 400, K from 2 to 7 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify22h-L03-L04/derive/rc_pathwise_check.py, output /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify22h-L03-L04/derive/rc_pathwise_check.out): non-largest additions 210: V_K unchanged in 210 of 210; V*_(K+1,j) >= V*_(K,j) for every draw in all 300 trials (0 violations); p-hat fell in 0 of 210. Control (d): when the added statistic is the largest, p-hat fell in 74 of 90 trials, so the claim needs the 'not the largest' condition. The span's clause 'such a poor alternative can make the Reality Check reject less often, never more' refers, through 'such', to a strategy whose statistic is not the largest; read pathwise (same data and draws) it is exactly (a)–(c). rows.check: 2.3-grade and 2.4-math (Roquain span, grade T with locator 'Theorem 2.5 (arXiv v3, 2020)')
rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L03.html line 409: Roquain and Verzelen show that an estimated null cannot always stand in for the true one: when the nulls are Gaussian with unknown mean and variance, a procedure that asymptotically matches Benjamini-Hochberg run with the true null exists if and only if the number of false nulls is of order less than N/log N, where N is the number of tests
rows.evidence: unchanged since a2a631a (git diff checked); round-24 evidence: Grade: T is the right grade for a result the paper proves with a precisely named theorem (BLUEPRINT section 3: 'proved on the page, or with a precisely cited proof'); the cited proofs are in the arXiv v3 PDF (dl/roquain_arxiv_v3/roquain_v3.txt). Theorem 2.5 (arXiv v3, p. 12 of the paper; image crop dl/roquain_arxiv_v3/thm25-11.png, 200 dpi, read): '(i) for a sparsity k_n >> n/log(n), there exists no (sequence of) AMO procedure that is AMO; (ii) for a sparsity k_n << n/log(n), the sequence of plug-in BH procedure (BH_alpha(theta~, sigma~)) is AMO, for the scaling (theta~, sigma~) given by standard robust estimators (13).' Section 2.7.2 restates it as dense (k_n >> n/log n) and sparse (k_n << n/log n) regimes. Attribution: 'Gaussian with an unknown rescaling parameters (mean and variance) and the alternative distribution is let arbitrary' (abstract) matches 'Gaussian nulls with unknown mean and variance'; the alternative is unrestricted in the paper, which the span does not say (scope is narrower than the paper, not wider; non-blocking). AMO (Definition 2.2) is 'asymptotically mimicking the oracle BH procedure': the span's 'asymptotically matches Benjamini-Hochberg run with the true null' is right. The 'if and only if ... of order less than N/log N' is the abstract's main-result sentence; at the level of orders it is proved: Theorem 3.1 (non-asymptotic lower bound: no procedure with FDR <= c3 is AMO when k2 >= c2 n log(2/alpha)(1+log(k2/k1))/log n) and Theorem 3.2 (plug-in BH is AMO when eta = c2 log(n/alpha)(k/n) v n^(-1/6) <= 0.05, i.e. k of order n/log n or below), so the boundary is order n/log n with constants. Theorem 2.5 itself is stated with >> and <<, so the locator should read 'Theorem 2.5; Theorems 3.1-3.2 (order-level constants)'. That is a precision suggestion, not a failure. Symbols: N is registered as local (notation/notation.json 'about': N is defined in each lesson), and the span defines it in the same sentence. Published-version numbering not verified (R22-cite-roquain2022false).
